problems.title: Quadrants of a decreasing line
problems.question: In which quadrants does y=-2.7x+3.6 lie?
problems.idea: Find its positive y-intercept and positive x-intercept.
steps: For x<0,y>0, so the line enters quadrant II.
For 0<x<4/3 it enters I; for x>4/3 it enters IV.
It never has x<0,y<0.

problems.title: Solve two linear equations
problems.question: x-y=2,3x+2y=21. Find xy.
problems.idea: Substitute y=x-2.
steps: 5x=25 gives x=5,y=3.
The product is 15.

problems.title: A vertical line is not a function y=f(x)
problems.question: A linear function’s graph lies in exactly two quadrants. Which listed pair I-II,I-III,I-IV,II-IV,III-IV is impossible?
problems.idea: Separate horizontal lines from lines through the origin.
formulas: A nonconstant nonvertical line through the origin has opposite quadrants; a nonzero constant has two upper or two lower quadrants.
steps: Horizontal positive and negative lines give I-II and III-IV.
Positive and negative slopes through the origin give I-III and II-IV.
The pair I-IV would require a vertical line x=c>0, which is not the graph of a function y=mx+b.

problems.title: An exterior angle is three times a smaller angle
problems.question: Extensions of chord AB and diameter DC meet at E, with B∈AE,C∈DE. BE equals the radius and AOD=57°. Find BEO.
problems.idea: Use BE=OB and OA=OB.
formulas: Equal sides give equal opposite angles; a triangle exterior angle equals its two remote interior angles.
steps: Let BEO=θ. In isosceles EBO, BOE=θ and OBE=180°-2θ.
Since BA is opposite BE, OBA=2θ. Then OAB=2θ as OA=OB.
AOD is the exterior angle of triangle AOE, so 57°=θ+2θ.

problems.title: Arc sum and difference from two chord angles
problems.question: Two secants meet outside at K and two chords meet inside at P. BPC=80°,BKC=10°. Find the smaller of minor arcs AD,BC.
problems.idea: The interior angle gives a sum; the exterior angle gives a difference.
steps: The two arc measures therefore sum to 160° and differ by 20°.

problems.title: A perpendicular line through an intersection
problems.question: Find the line perpendicular to the line through (2,2),(4,3), passing through the intersection of y=-x+8 and y=2x-1.
problems.idea: Find the point and required slope separately.
steps: The two given lines meet where -x+8=2x-1, giving (3,5).
A slope -2 line there is y-5=-2(x-3).

problems.title: Nonnegative summands must both vanish
problems.question: (a+4b-6)²+|3a-2b-4|=0. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Each term is nonnegative.
steps: Thus a+4b=6 and 3a-2b=4.
Substitute a=6-4b to get 18-14b=4, so b=1,a=2.

problems.title: Two price changes determine a budget
problems.question: If dolls were 2 lari cheaper Anna could buy 6 more; if 2 lari dearer she could buy 4 fewer. Find her money.
problems.idea: Let p be the usual price and q the usual quantity.
steps: The first equality gives q=3p-6, the second q=2p+4.
Hence p=10,q=24.
The budget is pq=240.

problems.title: A tangent cuts a fixed-perimeter corner triangle
problems.question: A radius-R circle touches both sides of a right angle at A,B. A tangent at a point on minor arc AB cuts off a triangle at the corner. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Equal tangent lengths replace the sloping side by two remaining leg pieces.
formulas: OA=OB=R; tangents from one exterior point are equal.
steps: Let the new tangent meet the angle sides at X,Y and touch the circle at T.
XT=XA=R-OX and YT=YB=R-OY.
Thus XY=2R-OX-OY, and OX+OY+XY=2R.

problems.title: A midpoint contact makes a small triangle equilateral
problems.question: D is the midpoint of the hypotenuse AB of right ABC. The incircle of ACD touches CD at its midpoint. Find the least angle of ABC.
problems.idea: A midpoint incircle contact forces the two other sides to be equal.
formulas: If the contact on CD is its midpoint, AC=AD; hypotenuse midpoint gives AD=CD.
steps: Thus ACD is equilateral, making CAD=60°.
Since D is on AB, A=60° and B=30°.

problems.title: Count small positive-coordinate pairs
problems.question: How many points with natural coordinates have coordinate sum 2,3 or 4?
problems.idea: For sum s and positive coordinates there are s-1 pairs.
steps: The sums contribute 1,2,3 pairs.
The total is 6.
problems.note: If natural numbers include 0, the count is 3+4+5=12. The printed answer 6 uses the positive convention.

problems.title: A midpoint follows from equally spaced ordinates
problems.question: A=(n,1),B=(3,7),C=(m,13) are collinear. Find n+m.
problems.idea: The middle ordinate is halfway between the other two.
formulas: B=(A+C)/2 because 7=(1+13)/2 on a straight line.
steps: Thus 3=(n+m)/2.
Multiply by 2.

problems.title: Use the first-third travel time to define the speed
problems.question: A car covers the first third of a route in 2 hours, then increases speed by 8 km/h and covers the rest in 3 h 36 min. Find the route length.
problems.idea: Let v be the first speed.
formulas: First-third distance=2v; remaining distance=4v; 3 h 36 min=3.6 h.
steps: The full route is 3·2v=432.

problems.title: Equal parallel chords form a rectangle
problems.question: Two equal parallel chords are distance R apart in a radius-R circle. Find the acute angle between their crossing joining chords AC,BD.
problems.idea: Their common distance to the centre is R/2.
steps: The four endpoints form a rectangle of width √3R and height R.
Its diagonals have direction vectors (√3R,R) and (√3R,-R).
Their acute-angle cosine is (3R²-R²)/(3R²+R²)=1/2.

problems.title: An incenter angle identifies the third vertex angle
problems.question: I is the incenter and AIC=144°. Find ABC.
problems.idea: Use the two internal bisectors.

problems.title: A divisor root gives the requested coefficient sum
problems.question: x⁴-3x³+5x²+Ax+B is divisible by x²-3x+2. Find A+B.
problems.idea: The divisor has root x=1.
steps: Set this to zero.

problems.title: Positive integer solutions of a linear equation
problems.question: Count natural pairs solving 2x+3y=30.
problems.idea: The parity condition forces y even.
steps: Positive y,x require k=1,2,3,4.
problems.note: If 0 were included, (15,0) and (0,10) would add two solutions. The printed count uses positive natural numbers.

problems.title: A square of three signed terms
problems.question: Expand (a-b-c)².
problems.idea: Treat b+c as one subtracted term.
steps: Set u=b+c and expand u²=b²+2bc+c².
The cross terms with a are -2ab and -2ac.

problems.title: Tangents from twice the radius away
problems.question: X is distance 2R from a circle centre O. XA,XB are tangents. Find AOB.
problems.idea: A radius is perpendicular to its tangent.
steps: Thus AOX=60°.
The symmetric triangle OBX gives XOB=60° as well.

problems.title: Choose the obtuse tangent-chord angle
problems.question: AOB is a central angle of 110°. C lies on the tangent at B and ABC is obtuse. Find ABC.
problems.idea: The two possible tangent-chord angles are supplementary.
steps: Its supplement is 180°-55°=125°.
The obtuse condition selects that value.

problems.title: Parallel slope through a given point
problems.question: Find the line through (3,5) parallel to the line through (1,7),(2,4).
problems.idea: Parallel lines have equal slopes.
steps: The required line is y-5=-3(x-3).
Expand.

problems.title: Axis-aligned legs identify the triangle
problems.question: Classify A=(1,3),B=(6,7),C=(1,7).
problems.idea: AC is vertical and BC horizontal.
formulas: AC=4; BC=5; vertical and horizontal lines are perpendicular.
steps: The right angle is at C.
The two legs differ, so the triangle is not isosceles.

problems.title: Recover old prices before applying the new ones
problems.question: Originally 2 kg apples and 3 kg pears cost 18 lari. Apples drop by one third and pears by 50%; now 4 kg apples and 5 kg pears cost 18. Find the new cost of 2 kg apples and 3 kg pears.
problems.idea: Let x,y be the old per-kilogram prices.
steps: Multiply the second equation by 6 to get 16x+15y=108.
Subtract five times the first: 6x=18, so x=3,y=4.
The new prices are 2 lari/kg each, so 2 kg plus 3 kg cost 10.

problems.title: Contact-chord angle in an incircle
problems.question: An incircle touches AB,BC,AC at K,M,N. If A=80°, find KMN.
problems.idea: The radii to K,N are perpendicular to the two sides at A.
formulas: Minor central angle KON=180°-A; inscribed angle equals half its intercepted arc.
steps: Thus the small arc KN away from M measures 100°.
Angle KMN intercepts that arc, so its measure is 50°.

problems.title: Intersecting circles bound their centre distance
problems.question: Two circles of radii 0.6 and 7.2 intersect. Their centre distance is an integer. Find it.
problems.idea: Use strict inequalities for two intersection points.
steps: Only integer 7 lies in that interval.
